releases.notes:
### Security

- **License verification now uses its own dedicated signing key**, separate from
  the key that signs software updates. Licenses issued before this release must
  be re-issued (no customer licenses were affected).

### Fixes

- **Showtimes board no longer hidden behind a poster.** After a movie shown with
  an animated poster and no trailer, the "Playing Soon" board could be covered by
  a blank, banner-less copy of that movie's poster for the whole showtimes
  duration. The board now displays correctly.
- **Animated posters play at the right speed on first show.** The first animated
  poster after the display starts up could run in slow motion (about half speed)
  at 4K; it now plays at full speed from the start.
- **Video slides play at the right speed too.** The same slow-motion problem
  affected video slides — the first time each one played after a restart or an
  update, it could run at about half speed. Slides now play at full speed
  immediately.
- **Trailers download in a format your Pi can play smoothly — without giving
  up quality.** Some trailers were being fetched in a video format the Pi 5
  cannot decode fast enough, causing stutter. htMarquee now prefers full-HD
  downloads it can play cleanly, and converts high-frame-rate trailers once at
  download time so they stay both sharp and smooth.
- **High-frame-rate trailers no longer play in slow motion.** Trailers at 50
  or 60 frames per second could play at roughly half speed on the display.
  They now play at normal speed — including ones already in your library.
- **The trailer list now shows only trailers you actually have.** A
  long-standing issue could mark alternate trailers as "downloaded" when they
  weren't, showing duplicate entries that all played the same video — and
  deleting one of them could remove a real trailer's file. The list now cleans
  itself up automatically on startup, and deleting a trailer can never remove
  another trailer's file.
- **Backups now remember your display orientation.** The screen-rotation
  setting wasn't included in backups, so restoring onto a new device could
  leave a rotated display back at its default orientation. Backups now capture
  it and restores apply it automatically.
- **Scheduled playlists stay in their date range after a restart.** A playlist
  limited to a season — a Christmas list, say — could briefly take over after a
  reboot even outside its dates. It now waits for its date window, restart or
  not.
- **The web app stays responsive while it works with images.** Uploading a
  banner, slide or format icon, or generating a colour theme from a poster,
  could briefly freeze the rest of the app and stall the display. That work now
  happens in the background.
- **Backup restore repairs your library again.** After restoring a backup, the
  automatic repair that re-fetches any missing poster or backdrop art was
  silently skipped; it now runs as intended.
- **TV power control is more reliable.** If an HDMI-CEC on/off command doesn't
  reach the TV on the first try (some TVs occasionally don't respond in time) —
  whether from the schedule or the power buttons — htMarquee now retries
  automatically instead of giving up.
- **Enabling HTTPS can no longer lock you out.** If HTTPS is turned on but its
  certificate is missing, htMarquee now stays reachable over plain HTTP instead
  of becoming unreachable.

### Security

- **Updated image and file-upload handling.** Picked up the latest security
  releases of the third-party libraries htMarquee uses to read uploaded images
  and receive file uploads.
- **The display no longer leaves local screen access open.** A permission needed
  only by a retired video playback path was being granted on every boot; it is
  now granted only if that path is actually in use.

### Dashboard

- New **Display Preview** card (Premiere): see exactly what's showing on your
  poster display, right from the dashboard. It refreshes every 30 seconds while
  you're viewing, a refresh button grabs an instant update, and clicking the
  image opens a larger view. Nothing is captured when you're not looking, and
  nothing is ever written to the SD card.
- Fixed the Now Showing card layout: long taglines and the cast list no longer
  spill outside the card — the cast is now a scrollable row.

### Network

- You can now manage the device's network from **Settings → Network**: set a
  static IP or use DHCP for the wired and Wi-Fi connections independently, and
  turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off.
- New **Prefer wired** option — when enabled, the device automatically falls back
  to Wi-Fi if the Ethernet connection loses internet, and switches back to wired
  when it returns.

### Display

- Fixed slow, jerky trailer playback (and a stray video box that could appear
  over a trailer). Trailers now play at full, smooth speed again.

### Reliability

- Your display's rotation is now kept across updates — updating no longer resets
  a portrait-mounted screen back to its default orientation.

### Performance

- Smoother Showtimes screen, and no brief stutter the first time a movie's
  trailer plays.

### Display

- The theater format badges (4K, Dolby Atmos, and the like) now sit in the
  bottom corners of the poster, so a long tagline no longer overlaps them.
- When you remove the last movie from the playlist, the display now shows the
  "add some posters" setup screen instead of leaving the removed movie's poster
  on screen.
- If a movie's animated poster can't be read, the display now falls back to its
  regular poster instead of showing a black panel.

### Reliability

- Refreshing a movie now updates the on-screen poster and trailer right away,
  instead of waiting for the next playlist cycle.
- The display recovers cleanly after a brief network drop — a previous movie's
  animated poster no longer lingers after it reconnects.
- Fixed a storage leak where removing cached movies left orphaned trailer files
  behind — automatic cleanup now reclaims the space it should.
- Background network and metadata tasks now recover from temporary errors
  instead of quietly stopping until the next restart.
- Faster startup on devices with large trailer libraries.

### Performance

- Lower memory use on the device, and smoother animated-poster and trailer
  playback — eliminated the repeated stutter when a title comes back around in
  the slideshow.

### Security

- Broad security hardening: a flood of wrong passwords can no longer lock the
  real owner out, and backups, server integrations, and the media library are
  better protected on shared networks.
- Hardened the on-device update process so it can only modify the app's own
  files.

### Web app

- The **Check for Updates** button no longer falsely reports you're on the
  latest version when your login session has expired.
- Fixed the mobile **Install App** button blanking the whole app. The app can
  now be installed to a phone's home screen; the button appears when your
  device trusts the display's security certificate.

### Other

- Added third-party attribution notices (TMDB, bundled fonts).

- The display recovers cleanly after a brief network drop — a previous movie's

- New **Vertical Position** option in Settings → Hardware → Display: choose
  whether your TV is rotated right (90°) or left (270°) into portrait. After
  changing it you'll be offered a display restart to apply the new position.

### Cache library

- Movie cards now show an **eye-off** badge for titles tied to a date-scoped
  playlist (hidden from regular rotation until that playlist is active) and a
  **spotlights** badge for titles with scheduled showtimes.
- New Cache filters — show only movies in regular rotation, tied to a
  date-scoped playlist, in any playlist, or with scheduled showtimes — and they

### Security & reliability

- Fixed a problem where restoring a backup could corrupt the movie
  database, leaving the device unable to load its library after the
  restore. Restores now complete cleanly.
- Internal security and reliability improvements.

- Showtimes that have already ended now clear themselves automatically within a
  few minutes, instead of lingering until the next change. The grace period
  after a showtime ends is now 1 hour.
- The "Schedule Showing" button has moved from the movie grid onto the movie
  detail view, where it opens pre-filled for that movie.

### Image Integrity

- htMarquee now records a fingerprint of every cached poster, backdrop, and
  trailer, so it can catch artwork that has gone wrong — for example a poster
  file that ended up showing the wrong movie — not just artwork that's missing.
- "Repair Library" now checks image content as well as presence, and a new
  "Rebuild Image Integrity" button re-downloads all artwork to fix corruption
  and refresh the fingerprints.

### Backups

- Backups and restores now verify file integrity, and the database is
  integrity-checked before a restore is trusted — so a corrupted backup is
  caught rather than restored over your working library.

### Display

- The DTS-HD Master Audio format badge is now legible on the display (it was
  rendering too dark to read against the background).
- Fixed a problem where the display could end up running twice after a restart
  or update, slowly increasing memory use over time. The display now runs as a
  single managed process.

### Trailers

- Trailers that were downloaded but silently never played (their length wasn't
  recorded) now play correctly, and any already in that state are repaired
  automatically.
- A trailer whose file has gone missing or can no longer be downloaded is now
  cleaned up automatically, so the display never tries to play a trailer that
  isn't there.

### Other

- Fixed the Dashboard "Playlists" count showing 0 when playlists existed.
- The Disk Usage bar now shows space used by backups as its own segment.
- Removed the QR code / Remote Access panel from Network settings.

### Showtimes

- The per-showing backdrop option is now labeled "Show a random backdrop each
  time" (previously "Cycle backdrops") so its effect is clearer.

### Reliability

- Software updates now apply automatically after you install them — previously an
  update could finish staging but not take effect until a manual restart.
- The "update available" prompt now shows and clears reliably.
- TV power and input status (HDMI-CEC) now update reliably in the web app.
- More robust trailer downloads.

### Showtimes

- With "Cycle backdrops" enabled, the Showtimes screen now shows a different
  backdrop every time it appears — previously it kept the same one until the
  next refresh.

### Updates, reliability & security

- More reliable software updates: an update that introduces a new dependency
  now installs it correctly.
- Stronger abuse protection on the login, setup, and license screens.
- Additional hardening of network configuration, dependency versions, and the
  release build pipeline.

### Reliability & Showtimes

- Editing a Showtime no longer silently turns off its "Cycle backdrops"
  setting — your choice now sticks when you change other fields.
- Enabling "Cycle backdrops" now reliably downloads the movie's alternate
  backdrops in the background (this had quietly stopped working).
- Steadier display: slideshow phase updates are no longer occasionally
  dropped, and playing a video Showtime or slide no longer causes a brief
  stall.
- The offline/online indicator and the live update-progress bar now
  refresh reliably.
- After a factory reset, a device with a custom name now redirects you to
  the correct address.

### Security & hardening

- The over-the-air update system now downloads over verified TLS and
  requires a matching checksum and signature before installing.
- Tightened the web app, settings, and backup/restore: stricter input
  validation, tighter TLS private-key permissions, and a size limit that
  rejects malformed restore archives.
- Reduced the background service's system privileges.

### Showtimes (Premiere)

- **Enable / disable Showtimes** — a new master switch at the top of
  the Showtimes settings panel turns the whole feature off without
  having to delete your scheduled entries. The Showtimes screen stops
  appearing in the slideshow until you turn it back on.
- **Cycle backdrops on each appearance** — a new checkbox on each
  Showtime entry. When enabled, the Showtimes screen rotates through
  every available backdrop for that movie (the primary plus every
  alternate) randomly each time it appears, so the same movie looks
  fresh across consecutive showings.
  - Enabling automatically downloads every TMDB backdrop for the movie
    in the background — no need to manually pick them one at a time.
  - Works alongside the existing "pick a specific backdrop" picker:
    leave cycling off for one specific image, turn it on when you want
    variety.

### Library Repair (new)

- **New: Repair Library** — htMarquee now self-heals missing posters
  and backdrops in your library, fixing a long-standing issue where the
  storage janitor could quietly delete cached image files and leave
  movies showing blank thumbnails on the marquee and in the web UI.
  - **Manual button** in Settings → Maintenance: scan your library and
    re-download anything missing. Shows live progress and a final
    "repaired N / failed N" summary.
  - **Automatic after a restore** — when a backup is restored from
    another device (or an older backup that didn't capture all
    images), the repair sweep runs automatically so the screen is full
    again without you having to do anything.
  - **Scheduled sweep** — Off / Daily / Weekly at a configurable hour
    (default weekly at 4 AM local).
- **Showtimes self-heal** — if the Showtimes screen finds a movie
  without a cached backdrop, it now silently queues a re-download in
  the background, so the next time that movie appears its backdrop is
  there.
- Posters were already self-healing in v1.1.6. Backdrops join now —
  same TMDB-CDN download path, same atomic write semantics.

### Showtimes (Premiere)

- **New: Showtimes** — a fullscreen interstitial that announces what's
  playing soon, perfect for upcoming-features signage in a home theater
  lobby.
  - New **Showtimes** tab lists upcoming movies; pick from your library or
    search TMDB to schedule a movie that isn't cached yet (the system
    caches it for you).
  - Each entry is one movie on one date, with up to **three show times**
    per date.
  - Up to **four movies per screen**, each on its TMDB backdrop image with
    slow Ken Burns motion. Title, date, and show times overlay the
    backdrop in consistent square-cornered badges.
  - **Auto-arranged layout** — if there are fewer than four upcoming
    showings, the screen centers them with a subtle warm bokeh
    cinema background filling the gaps.
  - **Configurable header** — your own text (e.g. "Playing Soon",
    "Upcoming Features"), font, color, and size. The header text
    auto-shrinks if it would overflow at the chosen size.
  - **Schedule controls** — choose how often the screen appears
    (every N posters), how far ahead to look (days), how long it stays
    on (5–30 seconds), and how long after a start time to keep a
    showing visible.
  - Movie cards now have an **Add Showtime** button to pre-fill the form
    for that movie.
  - Optional: pick an alternate backdrop from TMDB if you prefer a
    different image for a particular showing.
- **Library protection** — movies referenced by a Showtime are protected
  from being deleted by the library cleaner. Trying to delete such a
  movie surfaces a clear message listing the blocking Showtimes.

### Posters

- Missing or corrupted movie posters now re-download automatically in the
  background, filling in gaps without any manual action.

### Backups & Restore

- **New: choose how a restore handles posters already on the device.** The
  restore dialog now offers three modes:
  - **Reconcile** (default) — restore the backup's library and clear out
    leftover posters that aren't part of it.
  - **Merge** — keep both the current posters and the restored ones.
  - **Replace** — wipe existing posters and restore only the backup's.
- **Restoring onto a different device now explains the license status.**
  Licenses are tied to the original device, so a restored license shows as
  invalid on new hardware — you'll now see a clear message saying it's
  registered to a different device and needs reactivating, instead of a bare
  "invalid".

### Installation & Updates

- Fixed a bug where installing or updating on a Raspberry Pi with no Wi-Fi
  (Ethernet only) could stop before the display service started, leaving the
  screen offline. Ethernet-only devices now install and start reliably.

### Backups & Restore

- **Fixed a data-loss bug during restore.** A large backup could briefly fill
  enough of the SD card that the automatic storage cleanup kicked in and deleted
  cached movies mid-restore — on one cross-device restore it removed 112 of 276
  movies. Restores now pause the cleanup until they finish, don't count the
  in-progress backup file against free space, and protect just-restored movies
  from eviction.
- **Restoring onto a different device no longer changes that device's network
  settings — unless you want it to.** The restore dialog's "Keep current network
  settings" option (on by default) now genuinely preserves the target's IP,
  hostname, and mDNS name; before, it could silently leave them overwritten by
  the backup. Unchecking it still restores the backup's network settings — the
  right choice when replacing a dead device with an identical one.
- **Restore now checks free space first** and refuses with a clear message if the
  backup won't fit, instead of starting and failing partway through.
- Restoring a backup now ends with a clear "Restart Required" modal — one click
  restarts the server to finish applying any schema migrations added since the
  backup was taken.
- Restore and update progress now update reliably in the web UI while work is in
  progress.

### Display

- "Now Showing" on the dashboard now shows each movie's tagline instead of repeating the display banner text under every title.
- Fixed the time countdown and "ends at" text being cut off at the screen edge during Jellyfin/Plex playback — they're now inset from the edge.
- Fixed the tagline overlapping the "ends 12:07 PM" text on Jellyfin/Plex playback. The tagline now truncates with an ellipsis when it would collide with the side time text, and renders at full opacity once visible.
- Fixed the "Use as App Theme" button on a movie card doing nothing.

### Trailers

- Added a "Re-detect black bars" button under Settings → Trailers to re-evaluate every cached trailer's letterboxing. Useful when trailers slipped through the initial detection.
- Fixed black-bar detection on Debian Trixie — the ffmpeg 7 cropdetect filter needed more sample frames than the older pipeline gave it, so many trailers were silently passing through with bars intact. After installing the update, re-run "Re-detect black bars" once to fix existing trailers.
- Custom YouTube trailer downloads now report real success or failure. Previously, clicking "Download" on a pasted YouTube URL showed "Downloading custom trailer..." and that was the last you'd hear about it — there was no follow-up if the download actually finished or failed. Now you get a clear toast within ~30 seconds: a success message with the trailer duration, or an explanation if the video was unavailable / age-restricted / otherwise broken.
- Fixed "orphan trailer file" bug where a service restart in the narrow window between yt-dlp finishing a download and the DB commit could leave a fully-downloaded trailer file invisible to the app forever. The boot-time reconciliation now finds these orphans on every restart and links them back to the movie automatically (previously only resynced files for movies that already thought they had a trailer).

### Storage & performance

- Storage Janitor now defaults its cleanup thresholds to 51% of the SD card on a fresh install, so a full system backup always fits on the same card.
- Backend memory usage dropped by ~450 MB at idle. On 2 GB Pi hardware this keeps the system comfortably below the OOM line even during heavy trailer-processing bursts.
- **Fixed a data-loss bug** where the Storage Janitor would evict cached movies to "free up disk space" that was actually a user-created backup file. A 13 GB backup ZIP could trigger eviction of 100+ movies as collateral damage. The janitor now correctly excludes the backups directory from the disk-pressure calculation, and the Storage UI shows backup file size as its own category so you can see what's actually using disk.

### Library

- Movie lists now sort library-style: a leading "The", "A", or "An" is ignored when alphabetizing. *The Dark Knight* sorts under D, *An American Tail* under A(merican), etc. The full title still displays unchanged. Existing libraries get the new sort order automatically on update — no rebuild needed.

### Settings & Now-Cache UI

- Custom banner text now shows a live "N / 50" character counter that turns amber past 28 characters.
- Banner auto-fits font size to the message only when the message or font actually changes — manual slider tweaks are no longer overwritten on the next save.
- Better defaults for the trailer overlay: 12.5% vertical offset and 25% poster opacity during trailer playback.
- The Display Poster Resolution dropdown no longer loads blank on first open.
- Auto-cache defaults lowered to 5/day and 20 total (was 20/100) so the system uses less network bandwidth out of the box.
- Cache tab: genre chips no longer jammed against the movie grid (now spaced like the Discover tab), and the sort / rating / "favorites only" filters work again.
- Format-badge assign and delete buttons work again.
- Setting a preferred poster on a movie immediately updates the movie card image, not just the display.

### Integrations & auth

- HDMI-CEC enable toggle now shows a "Requires restart" hint and prompts you to restart immediately when you turn it on (instead of leaving the change in an "applied later" limbo).
- HTTPS↔HTTP protocol toggle no longer leaves you stuck on a login loop after the server restart.
- Matinee tier's 50-movie cap now shows a clear cap message instead of logging you out when you try to add the 51st.
- Pause-timeout setting (under Integrations) and the whole Playback Behavior section are now properly gated behind a Premiere license.
- License page redirect text fixed: "redirected to the htMarquee website" (was "Lemon Squeezy").
- License-request: now shown inline with Copy + Download buttons in a dark monospace box, sized to its content.
- Cert upload validates the uploaded cert against the existing private key before applying — gives specific error messages instead of a generic failure when the cert and key don't match.

### Hostname & network identity

- The setup wizard now has a "Pick a Name" step that lets you choose this device's network name (e.g. `htmarquee-livingroom.local`) instead of the default `htmarquee.local`. If another htMarquee is already on your network, the wizard warns you so you can pick something unique.
- Settings → Environment now shows a live availability check next to the mDNS Hostname and System Hostname fields — if the name you type is already claimed by another device on the LAN, you'll see a warning with the conflicting IP, but you can still save (useful when replacing an existing device).
- Hostname changes require a restart to take effect, same as port/HTTPS changes. The Settings UI prompts for the restart automatically.
- Fixed timezone and NTP-server changes silently not taking effect — the saved value was persisted but never applied to the OS clock until the next service restart, with no prompt. These now correctly trigger the "Restart required" banner like other env-config fields.

### Hardware

- Fixed CEC quick-panel buttons firing N times after switching tabs N times.

### Under the hood

- Substantial internal cleanup of the backend codebase. Feature routes moved into per-feature folders, startup logic extracted from main.py into a separate bootstrap module, and new pre-flight checks added so future releases catch obfuscation regressions sooner. No user-visible changes.

### Reliability

- Fixes fresh installs from htmarquee.com. The v1.1.0 release tarball was missing the bundled installer, so first-time installs failed partway through. Existing systems updating via OTA were not affected.

### Reliability

- OTA updates run in a separate background service. Update installs survive crashes or freezes that would previously have left the Pi in a half-installed state.
- Restoring backups is much more reliable, even very large ones. The restore pipeline runs in its own background service with isolated memory, so a heavy restore can't take down the rest of the Pi.
- The Restore-from-backup page now handles very large backups (8GB+) directly from the browser. The upload is automatically split into chunks so memory stays bounded regardless of backup size, and a single failed chunk retries instead of restarting the whole upload.
- Settings saves are faster and no longer collide with each other.

### Behind the scenes

- Significant internal restructuring for long-term maintainability.

### Behind the scenes

- **Frontend modularization completed.** The remaining feature code
  in the main `app.js` script — settings tabs, hardware controls,
  environment config, backup/restore, cache management, dashboard,
  and more — moved into dedicated per-feature modules. No user-visible
  change; the page loads and behaves identically.

### Fixes

- **Cleaner cache deletion.** Removing a cached movie — through the
  "Delete from cache" button, the broken-cache cleanup, or the
  block-a-movie flow — now also removes the movie's trailer metadata
  rows and any extra trailer variants the "Download All" button had
  previously downloaded. Before this fix, those entries were
  orphaned in the database and on disk.

- **Demo content survives reinstall.** If you deprovision and
  reinstall, the shipped demo movie (Big Buck Bunny) and demo slide
  now come back correctly. Previously the seed markers in the
  preserved data directory caused the seeder to skip, leaving
  orphaned media on disk.

### Behind the scenes

- **Frontend modularization continued.** Internal frontend modules
  now communicate exclusively through ES module imports — the last
  cross-feature `window.X` bridges between modules were retired.
  No user-visible change.

### Behind the scenes

- **Architecture cleanup, continued.** Settings saves now use per-key
  locks, removing a class of sporadic "database is locked" errors when
  multiple settings change at once. Internal websocket and
  state-machine contracts were tightened. No user-facing changes this
  release.

### Behind the scenes

- **Internal architecture cleanup.** Foundations for the next batch of
  features: a typed event bus, a declarative settings registry, and the
  start of frontend modularization. No user-facing changes this release.

### Fixes

- **Backups now capture the database accurately.** Previously a small
  number of recent changes could be missing from a backup, causing
  subtle inconsistencies after restore.
- **Backups now include the license file.** Restoring on a fresh Pi
  keeps your Premiere tier intact without re-uploading the license.
- **Trailer black-bar removal handles longer trailers reliably.**
  Previously trailers around three minutes or more could time out during
  analysis and skip the auto-crop step.
- **Variable-aspect trailers preserve their full image.** Modern trailers
  that shift aspect ratio mid-clip (IMAX expansion, anamorphic sequences)
  no longer get over-cropped — when the aspect varies, the crop is
  skipped or kept conservative so nothing important gets cut off.
- **Animated movie posters no longer flash to static before the next
  movie.** Previously, when an animated poster cycled to the next movie,
  the marquee briefly showed the static version of the same poster
  before the transition. The animated frame now holds smoothly through
  the crossfade.

### Fixes
- **Backups now capture the database accurately.** Previously a small number of recent changes could be missing from a backup, causing subtle inconsistencies after restore.
- **Backups now include the license file.** Restoring on a fresh Pi keeps your Premiere tier intact without re-uploading the license.

### Fixes
- **Self-healing posters.** When a movie's poster file is missing, the slideshow skips that movie cleanly (no blank frame) and re-downloads the poster in the background. The repaired poster appears on the next rotation.
- **Boot-time poster check.** On startup, htMarquee verifies every cached movie's poster file is present and re-downloads any that are missing.

- **HTTP ⇄ HTTPS protocol switch race:** toggling Enable HTTPS and clicking Restart no longer lands on "connection refused". The page now waits for the server to be fully ready before reloading on the new protocol.
